# Card — M3 guidance

<!-- Generated by apps/site/scripts/one-off/migrate-guidance.mjs. Do not edit by hand.
     The component pages carry the reference; this file carries the guidance. -->

## Web

### Features

Reach for a card when several pieces of information belong together and travel together: a product with its price and its action, a summary with its numbers, a person with their role. A card is a container, so it wants content that can stand alone — if the content only makes sense in context with what is around it, a divider or a heading is probably doing the job better. Cards are most legible in a grid, where their shared shape does the grouping for you.

### Usage

**Do**

- Use one card per subject with scan-first hierarchy: headline, supporting text, actions.
- Pick the variant by style alone — all three share legibility and function.
- Group related cards in grids, lists, or carousels at shared resting elevation.

**Don't**

- Don't force non-card content into cards — spacing, headlines, or dividers may serve better.
- Don't nest interactivity — directly actionable or container-with-actions, never both.
- Don't scroll inside cards — expand to reveal instead.

### Tokens

| Element | State | Token | Value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Elevated container | resting | comp.card.elevated | surface-container-low, level1, 12px |
| Filled container | resting | comp.card.filled | surface-container-highest, 12px |
| Outlined container | resting | comp.card.outlined | surface + outline-variant, 12px |

### Anatomy

| Part | Role |
| --- | --- |
| CardHeader | The title slot. Headline first, supporting text under it. |
| CardContent | The body. Holds flush content like images as well as prose. |
| CardActions | The action row. Carries `role="group"` so the actions announce as a set. |

### FAQ

**Which card variant?**

Style choice only: elevated for separation with shadow, filled for subtle separation, outlined for a visible boundary with the most emphasis.

## Native

### Features

Reach for a card when several things belong together and should read as one unit: an item and its actions, a summary and its detail. The three variants are Material 3's — `filled`, `outlined` and `elevated` — and the difference is how the card separates from what is behind it: a fill, a hairline, or a shadow. Choose the quietest one that works. `elevated` is the only one that raises, and it is also the one to use sparingly: a screen where every card is elevated is a screen with no hierarchy. The card is a `View`, so what goes inside is entirely yours.

### Usage

**Do**

- Use one card per subject with a scannable hierarchy — headline, supporting text, actions.
- Pick the variant by surface alone: filled, outlined, or elevated all carry the same content contract.
- Make a pressable card by putting the press in a child (`ListItem`), not on the card.

**Don't**

- Don't nest interactivity — directly actionable or container-with-actions, never both.
- Don't scroll inside cards — expand to reveal instead.
- Don't force non-card content into cards — spacing, headlines, or dividers may serve better.

### Tokens

| Element | State | Token | Value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Filled container | resting | theme.color.surfaceContainerHighest | surfaceContainerHighest, medium corners, level 0 |
| Outlined container | resting | theme.color.surface | surface with 1px outlineVariant border |
| Elevated container | resting | theme.color.surfaceContainerLow | surfaceContainerLow, level 1 (the family's raised row) |

### Anatomy

| Part | Role |
| --- | --- |
| CardHeader | The title slot. Headline first, supporting text under it. |
| CardContent | The body. Holds the content the card groups. |
| CardActions | The action row. A right-aligned row of real pressables; the row itself takes no role (`accessibilityRole="none"`), so each control announces on its own. |

### FAQ

**When is a card elevated?**

Material 3 tabulates two rows: filled and outlined rest at level 0, the elevated card at level 1. Elevation is the variant — there is no elevation prop.

**How does this differ from the web card?**

The three-variant contract and the 0/1 elevation split are identical. The native card is a `View` with kern-drawn fills (no global CSS), and pressability always lives in a child.
